title: Ephemeral checkpoints and resumable-segment protocol for disconnected streaming clients
creator: Nina Patel
description:
Problem: Client disconnects and timeouts during long-running streaming generations cause wasted GPU work, unpredictable costs, and poor UX. Current heuristics (fixed TTL + eager GC) either hold expensive partial outputs too long or discard resumable state too aggressively, breaking function-call workflows and structured-output atomicity.

Goals: 1) Allow safe, resumable continuations for clients that transiently disconnect (mobile, flaky proxies) without preserving indefinite GPU allocations. 2) Provide deterministic cleanup for abandoned partial generations to reclaim resources quickly. 3) Preserve atomicity guarantees for tool/function calls and structured output when resuming or aborting. 4) Maintain compatibility with existing SDKs and minimize surface-area change for users.

Design summary: Introduce ephemeral checkpoint segments and a resumable-segment token. When a generation enters a long-running state (heuristic: > 2s of active token emission or explicit large-seq request), the runtime emits periodic soft-checkpoints: lightweight, compressed metadata capturing the KV-cache cursor, generation cursor, deterministic RNG seed, and last structured-output fragment boundary. Each checkpoint is assigned a short-lived lease (default 45s) stored in the ephemeral metadata store (S3-ish tombstones with small TTL index) and referenced by a resumable token returned to the client as a final-stream trailer or via streaming-metadata frames.

Resume protocol: Clients that reconnect present their resumable token in the initial request (Resume-Token header or SDK param). The control-plane validates the token (HMAC with ephemeral KMS key rotated hourly), restores the KV-cache cursor and generator cursor into a warm slot, and then attempts a continuable generation with best-effort output deduplication using checkpoint boundary markers. If the token expired or was reclaimed, server responds with a structured status explaining partial-output availability and suggests a fall-back model variant for full rerun.

Backpressure and flow-control changes: 1) Soft urgency windows per-client: dynamic credits based on recently observed latency and token-rate; 2) Early-shed policy: when a client disconnects without resume token, the runtime transitions generation to a low-priority preemption lane and initiates fast compaction of intermediate KV cache to a snapshot that can be checkpointed or discarded; 3) Adaptive TTL: checkpoint lease length scales with expected resume probability (based on client tier, region, and historical reconnect rate).

Function-call and structured-output considerations: 1) Tool-invocation atomicity: function calls are only confirmed to the client once the tool-side acknowledgement is persisted and associated with a checkpoint boundary; resumable tokens will reference pending function invocations and include an idempotency vector so resumed runs do not double-invoke external tools. 2) Structured outputs use explicit framing markers so partial JSON objects are never returned as final: resumable checkpoints always record the most recent completed object boundary.

Security & privacy: Resume tokens do not contain PII or model internals, only opaque HMAC-wrapped pointers to ephemeral metadata. Tokens are single-use by default for high-security tiers (Dedicated/Private) and multi-use for hosted tiers with shorter expiration. KMS integration is required for token signing and for encrypting ephemeral metadata at rest.

Trade-offs and alternatives considered: 1) Keep-alive leases on GPUs (rejected): high cost and resource pinning. 2) Full re-run on reconnect (simple, but poor UX): rejected for large generations. 3) Centralized long-term resume store (rejected for compliance reasons): we opted for short-lived ephemeral tombstones combined with customer-configurable retention for Dedicated/Private.

Operational metrics to track: resume_rate, resume_success_rate, average_time_to_reclaim_after_disconnect, noop_reinvoke_rate (duplicate function invocations), checkpoint_storage_cost, per-token-latency-impact. Dashboards prototyped in console: streaming/resume and streaming/abandoned-generations.

Rollout plan: 1) Canary in hosted for low-volume tenants with resume disabled-by-default (2 weeks). 2) Soft launch enabling resume for PLG customers with explicit opt-in via Console toggle (4 weeks). 3) Beta for Dedicated with configurable TTLs and audit logging (6 weeks). 4) Private deployment docs + operator playbook (rotate KMS keys, purge policies).

Testing: Unit tests for token validation, integration tests for resume roundtrip with function calls (mocked tool), chaos tests simulating mid-stream disconnect, load tests to measure checkpointing overhead under steady token-rate.

References: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/STR/ephemeral-checkpoints; RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/421; Prototype server PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9876; Dashboard mock: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/streaming/resume-proto
comments: 2026-02-20 - Marco: Initial spike completed. Prototype checkpoint encoding implemented in runtime branch. Observed ~2.3% median p99 latency increase during checkpoint flushes; will optimize write batching.
2026-02-25 - SRE (Aisha): Add retention alert for ephemeral tombstones and quota guardrails. Recommend default max ephemeral storage per-tenant = 500MB/hr.
2026-03-01 - PM (Elliot): UX note: SDKs should expose resume token getter and automatic resume on reconnect. Add feature flag in Console for opt-in.
2026-03-05 - Security (Priya): Reviewed token format; require KMS envelope encryption and rotate signing keys hourly for hosted tier. For Dedicated, expose policy to opt into multi-use tokens.

2026-03-08 - QA (Jon): Found race when client presents resume token while original generation still finalizing; fix: canonical transition state to 'finalizing' that blocks resume until write complete. Added test case.
2026-03-12 - Marco: Implemented conflict resolution for pending function calls by adding per-invocation idempotency vector and persisted invocation journal. Ready for canary config.
